title: DW-029 batch 1: evidence three requirements that were built but never verifiable
objective: Start the DW-029 acceptance-criterion programme with a batch small enough to do impeccably, establishing the method the remaining batches follow. THE METHOD, stated once here: pick requirements that are ALREADY BUILT, write an acceptance criterion, and record a Met verdict with real evidence IN THE SAME BATCH - never leaving a Pending AC behind. That ordering is not stylistic. acs-met counts by retired_in and IGNORES lifecycle_status, so an AC written ahead of its evidence holds package readiness false until that evidence exists; a bulk pass over all 135 would therefore make the package permanently un-ready, which is why DW-029 says it must not be run as one. THE SECOND RULE: verify the WHOLE criterion, not the part that is convenient. Both NFRs in this batch carry a 'Target:' clause stronger than the tests that existed - NFR-020's '0 unauthenticated non-health endpoints' was covered by three spot checks, and FR-151's eight named fields were covered by seven assertions. Where the evidence fell short of the requirement, the batch BUILT THE MISSING CONTROL rather than writing an AC around what happened to be tested. THE THIRD RULE, learned in batch 3 and settled by batch 9: a requirement that is only PART-verifiable gets a deferred-work row, NOT an acceptance criterion - an AC recording Partial holds readiness false permanently. STATUS NOTE, REWRITTEN AT CLOSE 2026-08-20: this slice ran twenty batches and is now Implemented, ACCEPTED BY THE OPERATOR on 2026-08-20. It was held at Approved throughout on the grounds quoted here for most of its life - that done-claiming a multi-batch programme is manufactured status - and it moves only because the OPERATOR DEFINED THE END CONDITION in an interview on 2026-08-20: done when only externally-blocked requirements remain. That condition is met. TWO Must-priority non-functional requirements are left and NEITHER can be closed by work in this repository: NFR-018 needs an external OWASP ASVS 5.0 Level 2 assessment, and NFR-038 rides Tarseem, whose phase P14 was deferred INDEFINITELY by DEC-028 and which has no endpoint in the product at all. Everything else is Met, carried by a deferred-work row with an activation trigger, or Deferred by scope change. WHAT Implemented MEANS HERE, since the store guards it: VERIFIED. Slice readiness passed every blocking rule - acs-met, wbs-done and defects-closed - with only the defects-minor advisory failing on DEF-100, which DEC-066 carries deliberately because the operator kept NFR-019 as a target rather than narrowing it. The verification Implemented requires is the OPERATOR'S ACCEPTANCE, and nothing mechanical could have supplied it for a programme slice: no gate can judge whether twenty batches of acceptance-criterion work were done well. THE PROGRAMME'S YIELD WAS NEVER ONLY VERDICTS - fourteen requirements were found built on one side only, each invisible precisely BECAUSE it had no criterion to fail, and the register now carries them as deferred-work rows with activation triggers instead of as silence.

WHY THESE FOUR AND NOT THE OTHER NINE. Each one's hard part is already done and only a thin surface is missing. DW-061 (NFR-063) needs one bilingual string pair and a breakpoint-guarded banner - the no-broken-layout half of that requirement is already plausibly met by real breakpoints at 900, 860, 760, 720 and 560 px across 27 stylesheets, so what is missing is an explanation, not a working page. DW-032 needs the existing Topic.Reclassify domain method reached from production code; it is deliberately unreachable today and its guard is disjoint from Convert's, so no topic can ever be a candidate for both.

THE ACCEPTANCE-CRITERION RULE THIS SLICE FOLLOWS, and it is not optional. Write the criterion and record its verdict in the SAME batch that produces the evidence, or do not write the criterion. acs-met counts by retired_in and ignores lifecycle_status, so a criterion written ahead of its evidence holds package readiness false permanently. If a row turns out to be only part-buildable, it gets a deferred-work row rather than a Partial verdict.

WHAT THIS SLICE DEMONSTRATES BEYOND ITS FEATURES: its work items are the first in this package to carry a real slice_id, which is the DEC-068 d2 fix-forward rule for DEF-087 in practice. All 155 pre-existing wbs_items have slice_id NULL, which is why slice-scope wbs-done could never fail for any of the 28 closed slices. This slice's exit is therefore the first one that rule can actually adjudicate.
